issues.failure_explanation: In testing the homogeneous problem with $w(t) = e^{-t/T} \partial_t \psi(t)$, the inner product $(\partial_t \psi, w)_{J_T}$ is purely real according to (3.5). Multiplying by $\mi$ yields a purely imaginary number whose real part is zero, not the positive integral $\int_0^T |\partial_s \psi(s)|^2 e^{-s/T} \dd s$. Furthermore, even if the displayed identity were valid, when $\mu < 0$ the right-hand side is a difference of non-negative terms, which does not imply $\psi \equiv 0$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the uniqueness argument by testing with $w = \psi$ and taking the imaginary part $\text{Im}(\mi (\partial_t \psi, \psi)_{J_T} + \mu (\psi, \psi)_{J_T}) = \text{Re}(\partial_t \psi, \psi)_{J_T} = \frac{1}{2} |\psi(T)|^2 = 0$, or use an integrating factor directly.
issues.overall_effect: The uniqueness proof for the continuous initial value problem in Proposition 3.2 is invalid as written, although the statement itself is true.
issues.title: Uniqueness proof of Proposition 3.2 uses invalid real-part evaluation and sign reasoning
issues.why_classification: A standard, one-line energy or integrating factor argument establishes uniqueness without altering any other results in the paper.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In particular, from these expressions, both $q^{\B^p}$ and $q^{\bC^p}$ are reciprocal polynomials, and from \eqref{eq:25}, it follows that $q^{\K^p(\rho)}$ is also a reciprocal polynomial for all $\rho \in \R$.

issues.failure_explanation: The polynomial $q^{\mathbf{C}^p}$ is anti-reciprocal ($q^{\mathbf{C}^p}(1/z) = -z^{-2p} q^{\mathbf{C}^p}(z)$) because the Toeplitz part of $\mathbf{C}_n^p$ is skew-symmetric. As a result, the linear combination $q^{\mathbf{K}^p(\rho)}(z) = \mi q^{\mathbf{B}^p}(z) - \rho q^{\mathbf{C}^p}(z)$ has complex coefficients satisfying $a_{2p-j} = -\overline{a_j}$. It is self-inversive/conjugate-reciprocal ($q^{\mathbf{K}^p(\rho)}(1/\overline{z}) = -\overline{z}^{-2p} \overline{q^{\mathbf{K}^p(\rho)}(z)}$), which pairs roots $\xi \leftrightarrow 1/\overline{\xi}$, rather than a reciprocal polynomial pairing $\xi \leftrightarrow \xi^{-1}$.

failure_location.quote: The symbol polynomial $q^{\mathbf{K}^p(\rho)}$ of the family $\{ \K_n^p(\rho) \}_n$ defined in \eqref{eq:21} is a reciprocal polynomial.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the property as conjugate-reciprocity / self-inversion, observing that roots are symmetric with respect to circle inversion $\xi \mapsto 1/\overline{\xi}$, which preserves the required root distribution type $(\ell, 2p - 2\ell, \ell)$.
issues.overall_effect: The root symmetry argument used to establish that $q^{\mathbf{K}^p(\rho)}$ is of type $(\ell, 2p - 2\ell, \ell)$ relies on a false premise and an incorrect polynomial symmetry definition.
issues.title: Proposition 3.8 incorrectly asserts that the symbol polynomial is reciprocal
issues.why_classification: Circle inversion $\xi \mapsto 1/\overline{\xi}$ preserves the equal count of roots inside and outside the unit circle ($|\xi| < 1 \iff |1/\overline{\xi}| > 1$), so the weakly well-conditioning proof survives intact once the symmetry is correctly stated.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma A.1 only bounds $\kappa(\mathbf{S})$ in terms of $\kappa(\mathbf{M})$, showing that stability of $\mathbf{M}$ implies stability of its Schur complement $\mathbf{S}$. In Theorem 4.2, this proves that $\mathbf{S}_w = \mathbf{S}_s$ is weakly well-conditioned. However, to conclude that the wave equation formulation (4.2) is stable, one must bound $\kappa(\mathbf{M}_w)$ in terms of $\kappa(\mathbf{S}_w)$. That reverse implication is asserted without proof or supporting estimate.

failure_location.quote: Hence, the weakly well-conditioning of these Schur complements implies the stability of formulation \eqref{eq:30} for all $p \in \mathbb{N}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Provide an upper bound on $\|\mathbf{M}_w^{-1}\|$ using the explicit block inversion formula $\mathbf{M}_w^{-1} = \begin{pmatrix} \mathbf{B}^{-1} - \mu_w \mathbf{B}^{-1} \mathbf{C} \mathbf{S}_w^{-1} \mathbf{C} \mathbf{B}^{-1} & -\mathbf{B}^{-1} \mathbf{C} \mathbf{S}_w^{-1} \\ \mu_w \mathbf{S}_w^{-1} \mathbf{C} \mathbf{B}^{-1} & \mathbf{S}_w^{-1} \end{pmatrix}$, showing that $\|\mathbf{M}_w^{-1}\|$ grows polynomially in $1/h$ because $\|\mathbf{B}^{-1}\|$, $\|\mathbf{S}_w^{-1}\|$, and $\|\mathbf{C}\|$ do.
issues.overall_effect: The unconditional stability guarantee for the wave equation discretization in Theorem 4.2 has a logical gap.
issues.title: Missing converse bound from Schur complement to full matrix conditioning in Theorem 4.2
issues.why_classification: The block inversion formula bounds $\|\mathbf{M}_w^{-1}\|$ in terms of the already established polynomial bounds on $\|\mathbf{S}_w^{-1}\|$ and $\|\mathbf{B}^{-1}\|$, closing the gap routinely without changing the theorem's statement.

issues.failure_explanation: Algorithm 1 claims to solve system (5.1). However, Step 4 solves with the operator $(\mathbf{R}_{h_t}^p \otimes \mathbf{A}_{h_{\bx}} + (\mathbf{R}_{h_t}^p)^{-1} \otimes \mathbf{M}_{h_{\bx}})$, which includes an extraneous $(\mathbf{R}_{h_t}^p)^{-1}$ factor copied from solvers for the wave equation. When unwound, Algorithm 1 actually solves $(\mathbf{B}_{h_t}^p (\mathbf{C}_{h_t}^p)^{-1} \mathbf{B}_{h_t}^p \otimes \mathbf{M}_{h_{\bx}} + \mathbf{C}_{h_t}^p \otimes \mathbf{A}_{h_{\bx}}) \boldsymbol{\Psi}_{\bh}^p = \mi \mathbf{F}_{\bh}^p$, which does not coincide with (5.1).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Step 4 with solving $(\mathbf{R}_{h_t}^p \otimes \mathbf{A}_{h_{\bx}} + \mathbf{I}_{h_t} \otimes \mathbf{M}_{h_{\bx}}) \boldsymbol{Z}_{\bh}^p = -\mi \boldsymbol{Y}_{\bh}^p$, eliminate the calculation of $(\mathbf{R}_{h_t}^p)^{-1}$ from Step 1, and set $\boldsymbol{\Psi}_{\bh}^p = (\mathbf{Q}_{h_t}^p \otimes \mathbf{I}_{h_{\bx}}) \boldsymbol{Z}_{\bh}^p$ in Step 5.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm 1 does not deliver the stated solution to the space-time linear system (5.1).
issues.title: Algorithm 1 solves an erroneous linear system due to an extraneous Schur factor
issues.why_classification: The solver algorithm as written fails its input-output contract, but the repair is a self-contained algebraic adjustment of the Bartels-Stewart transformation for (5.1).
